A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same PQMass research, with readable main text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices A–I. Matching content across page moves supports a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v2 reports original null tests, sampling-method evaluations, generative-model assessments, ablations, and permutation-test results in Section 3 and the appendices.

after.justification: v3 retains these original empirical results, including the numerical comparisons and the permutation experiment in Figure 23.

M1.justification: The Voronoi partitioning, count statistic, p-value formulas, and retessellation procedure remain unchanged. Appendix I expands the explanation of permutation calibration already present in v2; it does not introduce a new algorithm.

E1.justification: Both versions retain the same synthetic distributions, image datasets, time-series task, Adult Census data, astrophysical datasets, and protein-sequence comparisons. Appendix I retains the same Gaussian null and scaled-distribution scenarios.

E2.justification: The corresponding experiments retain the same comparison methods, including Wasserstein distance, MMD, JSD, FID, FLD, novelty metrics, and Schilling's weighted and unweighted tests. Energy distance is newly discussed and cited, but is not added to an empirical comparison.

E3.justification: Reported experimental settings and protocols are retained. Figure 23 still uses 100-dimensional Gaussian data, 1,000 samples per input, and a 1.1 scaling for the alternative; its permutation procedure already appeared in v2.

E4.justification: The region-count and distance-metric ablations, mode-dropping, noise-sensitivity, memorization, and permutation analyses are retained. Appendix I explains the existing Figure 23 more extensively without adding an analysis or experiment.

E5.justification: Repeated-run counts, standard-deviation reporting, and significance calculations remain unchanged. Permutation calibration of the mean across retessellations was already reported in v2; v3 does not establish a new uncertainty-estimation practice.

E6.justification: The numerical tables and plotted results are unchanged. For example, Table 6 retains p-values 0.5596 and 0.7055, and Figure 23 retains 0.58 for the null case and 0.02 for the scaled alternative. The rewritten discussion interprets these existing results.

T1.justification: Equations, assumptions, Propositions 2.1–2.2, and their proofs are retained. Some prose references change from 'Prop.' to 'Theorem' without changing the statements. Appendix I restates permutation calibration rather than supplying a new mathematical derivation.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same central claims about likelihood-free evaluation, fidelity, diversity, novelty, computational efficiency, and operation without feature extraction or auxiliary model fitting.

C2.justification: Appendix I newly emphasizes why permutation calibration can reject an alternative missed by the broader chi-squared reference and recommends it when initial retessellations are inconclusive. It also calls single-tessellation testing exact and removes v2's warning that averaging discards distribution-shape information, including the recommendation to inspect the histogram.

D1.justification: Model hyperparameters in Appendix D, hardware and timing information in Appendix F.5, and code/data access information are retained. Appendix I's expanded description of pooled-data permutations explains the existing procedure without adding concrete implementation settings.

R1.justification: v3 adds Good (2013) on permutation tests and Székely et al. (2004) on energy-distance testing. Appendix I also positions PQMass as computationally cheaper than the latter test, a limited addition to the prior-work comparison.

P1.justification: Appendix I is locally rewritten and expanded, while the broader narrative and section order remain stable. The author block adds equal-contribution information and a second correspondence address; proposition references also receive wording changes.

P2.justification: Figure 19 moves from page 24 to page 23, and Table 6 from page 26 to page 25, accompanied by spacing and text-flow adjustments. The figures, table structures, axes, legends, and substantive captions are otherwise retained.

improvement.justification: Appendix I explains the existing permutation procedure and Figure 23's power benefit more clearly. However, it removes the distribution-shape caution and newly calls a single-tessellation test exact, while Section 3.1 still describes its chi-squared calibration as approximate. These gains in explanation and losses in qualification leave the net effect on statistical clarity uncertain; the experiments and proofs provide no additional resolution.
